details: Following the US midterm elections, a sharp sell-off in US technology and AI-related stocks spilled over into cryptocurrency markets on November 5th and 6th, 2026. This decline was fueled by investor concerns that a Democratic-controlled Congress might introduce tighter regulations on artificial intelligence and slow down data center expansion. Bitcoin fell below $75,000, and Ethereum also saw significant losses, leading to over $1 billion in leveraged crypto positions being liquidated.
title: US Tech Stocks Plunge, Triggering Over $1 Billion in Crypto Liquidations

details: The US Nonfarm Payrolls report for October 2026 significantly surpassed expectations, with 165,000 new jobs added, more than double the forecast. This strong employment data typically signals to investors that the Federal Reserve may maintain higher interest rates for longer, or even consider another rate hike in December. Higher interest rates tend to make conservative investments more attractive, potentially diverting capital from risk-on assets like cryptocurrencies.
title: US Jobs Report Exceeds Forecasts, Raising Rate Hike Speculation

details: The US Treasury Department's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) and the Federal Reserve Board of Governors have withdrawn a proposed "Travel Rule" that would have lowered the reporting threshold for cryptocurrency transactions to $250. This proposal, initially introduced in 2020, aimed to require financial institutions to collect and retain information on smaller crypto transfers. The withdrawal is seen as a positive development for the cryptocurrency industry by crypto advocacy groups.
title: FinCEN Rescinds Lowered Crypto Transaction Reporting Threshold

details: Christine Lagarde, President of the European Central Bank (ECB), announced her resignation effective February 7, 2027. The Eurogroup has received two nominations for her successor: Pablo Hernández de Cos (Spain) and Klaas Knot (Netherlands). The Eurogroup is scheduled to discuss these candidacies at its upcoming meeting on November 9, 2026. Changes in central bank leadership can introduce uncertainty or shifts in monetary policy, which may indirectly influence global financial markets and, consequently, cryptocurrencies.
title: ECB President Lagarde to Resign; Two Candidates Nominated

details: Global markets are currently grappling with persistent uncertainty regarding the growth outlook and expectations that inflation will remain elevated into next year. Although oil prices have eased recently, they remain significantly higher year-to-date, contributing to sustained inflationary pressures. This scenario could compel central banks to consider further interest rate hikes, even as economic growth slows, creating a challenging environment for financial assets, including cryptocurrencies.
title: Global Markets Weigh Elevated Inflation, Softening Growth Outlook
